      - heading "Understand Angles in the Same Segment" [level=2]
  - text: CLASS 10 · CIRCLE PROOFS
  - heading "Angles in the Same Segment" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Angles standing on the same chord in the same segment of a circle are equal.
  - text: 30 min RIGOROUS PROOF geometry2d
  - navigation:
    - button "Interact"
    - button "Learn"
    - button "Example"
    - button "Formula"
    - button "Practice"
  - main:
    - heading "Explore the theorem" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Drag points C and D along the circle.
    - complementary:
      - img
      - text: Result
      - strong: ∠ACB = ∠ADB
      - text: The angles are equal.
      - paragraph: ∠ACB 52.0°
      - paragraph: ∠ADB 52.0°
      - paragraph: Difference 0.0°
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: C and D may move anywhere on the circle. Their chord-side relation drives the result.
    - article:
      - button "Reset":
        - img
        - text: Reset
      - button "Open diagram full screen":
        - img
        - text: Full screen
      - img "Two draggable angles standing on chord AB":
        - text: Chord Tangent Angle O ∠AOB = 104.0° A B
        - slider "Point C on circle"
        - text: C
        - slider "Point D on circle"
        - text: D 52.0° 52.0°
    - heading "Why this is true" [level=2]
    - paragraph: The central angle subtended by chord AB is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same chord in the same segment.
    - paragraph: So ∠ACB = ∠ADB = ½ ∠AOB = ½ × 104.0° = 52.0°.
    - article:
      - heading "Worked Example" [level=2]
      - paragraph: In the figure, AB is a chord of a circle with centre O. ∠ACB = 58°. Find ∠ADB.
      - text: C D A B
      - paragraph: Solution
      - paragraph: Since C and D lie on the same segment of chord AB,
      - strong: ∴ ∠ADB = 58°
    - article:
      - heading "Common Misconception" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: Common Misconception
      - paragraph: Points on opposite segments do not give equal angles.
      - paragraph: They give supplementary angles.
      - text: C D A B
      - strong: If C and D lie on opposite segments of AB, then ∠ACB + ∠ADB = 180°.
    - article:
      - heading "Quick Check" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Move C and D independently. What happens to the angles?
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: Same segment ∠ACB = ∠ADB
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: Opposite segments ∠ACB + ∠ADB = 180°
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: Press Arrow Down on a point to cross the chord.
    - heading "Your Challenge" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Drag points C and D anywhere on the circle. Classify the relationship between the angles.
    - button "Equal (same segment) ∠ACB = ∠ADB"
    - button "Supplementary (opposite segments) ∠ACB + ∠ADB = 180°"
    - text: "Goal: Observe when the relationship changes and explain why."
